newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close easier ahead of settlement.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close easier ahead of settlement.

text.p: French stocks closed slightly lower on Friday in profit-taking ahead of the monthly settlement on Monday, traders said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished down 2.87 points, or 0.14 percent, at 2,079.46, off its session lows, while the CAC-40 September futures contract fell six points to 2,082.50.
For the week, the CAC index was down 0.4 percent as the bourse consolidated its strong previous gains.
Volume on Friday was 4.23 billion francs.
* Pernod-Ricard was the biggest loser on the CAC 40, shedding 5.28 percent to 278.30 francs.
Several brokerage houses lowered their ratings and earnings forecasts for Pernod-Ricard after the drinks group reported a drop in first-half operating profit on Thursday evening.

Portfolio managers said SGE Delahaye cut its rating to underperform from outperform on the share, Paribas Capital Markets cut its rating to hold from buy, Leven to reduce from buy and Exane to reinforce from buy. They said Leven and Paribas cut their earnings forecasts.
* Aluminium group Pechiney finished up 3.50 francs at 216.80 after announcing plans to lower costs by four billion francs, including axing between 4,000 and 5,000 jobs worldwide.
* Insurer AGF closed up 1.50 francs at 140, partly recouping Thursday's fall after announcing first-half results, which were sharply higher after capital gains.
* Saint Gobain finished 2.28 percent lower at 643 francs after saying it expected flat 1996 pre-exceptional results. "The market is a little disappointed," one trader said.
